sections.h2: Selling in Middletown Township, Bucks County
sections.html:
Middletown Township requires a Level 2 chimney inspection on every home that is sold, and Levittown sections add a heater compartment wall inspection. That fire marshal rule is the main local step. After it comes the 2 percent transfer tax, which you pay when the deed is filed.

The township has about 46,040 residents spread across roughly 19 square miles. It surrounds the boroughs of Langhorne, Langhorne Manor, Penndel and Hulmeville, which is why many addresses read Langhorne even though they sit in the township. Other Pennsylvania townships share the Middletown name, so make sure you are looking at the Bucks County one.

Whether you list, sell on your own or take a cash purchase, the township rules below still apply.

The mix of housing shapes how buyers see a sale. Levittown sections in the south were built in the 1950s, with hundreds of similar homes per development. Parkland has houses from every decade of the 20th century and the 21st. Newer townhouses and condominiums cluster around the Oxford Valley Mall, alongside assisted living and 55-plus housing, and a few older farm properties remain.

Neshaminy School District serves the township, and buyers regularly want to know the elementary zone for a given street. Interstate 295 skirts the eastern side, and U.S. Route 1 cuts through the middle. Commuters can use Woodbourne station on SEPTA's West Trenton line, or Langhorne station just over the border. Basements and drainage are a fair question for any buyer inspection, so keep repair records handy.

sections.h2: Chimney inspection when a house sells
sections.html:
Every home sold in the township needs a Level 2 chimney inspection, and the Fire and Emergency Management office keeps a copy. The rule follows NFPA 211, which calls for the inspection any time a property is sold or transferred.

The inspection covers any appliance that vents combustion gases, including oil-fired and gas-fired heaters with a metal B-vent chimney, fireplaces, wood stoves and pellet stoves. A certified CSIA chimney sweep must do it, and the township website keeps a courtesy list of local sweeps. A home with only electric heating and cooling, or one whose fireplace is vent-less, is outside the rule, and plastic PVC exhaust pipe is also exempt from a Level 2 inspection.

Middletown Township resale requirements and costs
RequirementWhat to know
Level 2 chimney inspectionRequired for homes with combustion appliances, done by a CSIA sweep
Levittown extra stepHeater compartment wall inspection
Transfer tax2 percent total, paid at recording
Statement of valueState form REV-183, in duplicate
Fire marshal office215-750-3812

The 2026 combined millage is 252.2674 mills. Three taxing bodies make up that number: the county at 29.65 mills, the Neshaminy School District at 198.0124 mills and the township at 24.605 mills.

The township's own 24.605 mills break down into a general fund of 7.025, a debt service fund of 5.115, fire protection of 4.75, parks and recreation of 3.25 and fire apparatus of 2.5, plus smaller street light, ambulance, road machinery and hydrant levies. A mill works out to one dollar of tax per thousand dollars of assessed value. Assessed values come from the Bucks County Board of Assessment, and Neshaminy's share is the bulk of the total.

On a Middletown sale the recorder collects 2 percent: half goes to the state and half is shared by the municipality and school district. You pay at recording, and the taxable value is not always the sales price.

The law does not assign the cost, and buyers and sellers usually split it. If too little was paid, the new owner answers for the difference. Since January 2026 the recorder has refused personal checks, and accepts only cash at the office, a cashier's check, a money order or a credit card, so alert your title company.

  • Exemptions can cover transfers among spouses, parents and children, grandparents and grandchildren, and siblings.
  • Former spouses may make one such transfer.
  • A deed for $1, or any transfer where no tax is paid, needs a statement of value so the state can check what the property is worth.

Exemption questions go to the recorder's office at 215-348-6209.

Early August is the yearly appeal deadline, and a successful appeal changes the bill starting the next tax year. Hearings are held at 55 East Court Street in Doylestown, at 10 a.m. on the first and third Tuesdays of every month, and the phone number is 215-348-6219. The county website posts forms and rules for residential and commercial properties.

Two more county items touch buyers and sellers. You apply for the homestead and farmstead exclusion by March 1 for the tax year that begins the next July 1. Under Act 29, someone who buys must send the Board of Assessment their contact information within 30 days.

sections.h2: Getting through the inspection and closing
sections.html:
Hire a CSIA chimney sweep the moment you decide to sell. Ask the sweep to check every vented appliance, including any fireplace or stove, and send the report to Fire and Emergency Management. If the report finds a problem, you will want time to repair it before settlement. In a Levittown section, call the fire marshal at 215-750-3812 and ask what the heater compartment wall inspection involves.

In the meantime, confirm with your title company how the transfer tax will be paid, because the recorder takes no personal checks. When the deed shows no price, the REV-183 statement of value goes in twice. At the table, compare the tax split and the school and township proration with your contract.

sections.h2: Is a listing or a cash sale the better fit in Middletown?
sections.html:
Deferred repairs point toward a cash sale, and a house a lender will finance as it stands points toward a listing. Either way, the chimney inspection comes first, and a failed inspection can change what you can ask.

  • Book a CSIA chimney sweep before you list and send the report to the fire marshal.
  • If the house is in Levittown, ask the fire office what the heater compartment wall inspection involves.
  • Compare offers after the 2 percent transfer tax, your mortgage payoff and the school and township tax proration.

Cash Home Buyers CA can give you a figure to compare with a listing.

faqs.q: Does Middletown Township require a chimney inspection when I sell?
faqs.a: Yes. A Level 2 chimney inspection by a certified CSIA sweep is required for homes with combustion appliances, and a copy goes to Fire and Emergency Management. Levittown homes also need a heater compartment wall inspection.

faqs.q: What is the transfer tax in Middletown Township?
faqs.a: The Bucks County Recorder of Deeds lists 2 percent in total: 1 percent to the state and 1 percent to the municipality and school district. The tax is paid at the time of recording.

faqs.q: Which school district serves Middletown Township?
faqs.a: Neshaminy School District. Five elementary schools, two middle schools and Neshaminy High School serve the township.

faqs.q: What is the total property tax rate in Middletown Township?
faqs.a: The 2026 combined rate is 252.2674 mills: 29.65 for the county, 198.0124 for Neshaminy School District and 24.605 for the township.

faqs.q: When can I file a Bucks County assessment appeal?
faqs.a: Annual appeals are due in early August. Call the Board of Assessment at 215-348-6219 with questions about the process.
